topic: The Geometric Relationship: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow

sections.title: Prerequisite Visualization: The Cross-Section
lecture_lines: A sphere is a perfectly round 3D shape.
A flat plane slicing through creates a circle.
This circle is the sphere's cross-section.
animations: Show a 3D sphere object in #FFFFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Rotate the sphere [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] slowly to show depth.
Highlight the central cross-section plane in #FFD700 within the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].

sections.title: The Projection Principle: Orthographic Shadows
lecture_lines: Parallel rays project a sphere's shadow.
The shadow is a circle of radius r.
Its area formula is simply pi r squared.
animations: Draw a sphere using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] in #FFFFFF and parallel light rays.
Show rays casting a circular shadow on a plane using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] to represent the projection.
Highlight the shadow circle in #00FFFF with its area.

sections.title: Linking Shadow to Surface Area
lecture_lines: Archimedes discovered a remarkable geometric truth.
The sphere's surface area is four pi r squared.
This equals exactly four times the shadow's area.
Visualize a cylinder wrapping around the sphere.
The cylinder's surface area matches the sphere's.

sections.title: Application: The Solar Power Challenge
lecture_lines: Consider a spherical satellite in space.
It only intercepts sunlight via its projected shadow.
Surface area is larger than this interception area.
animations: Show a spherical satellite [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg] intercepting sunlight [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sun.svg].
Display shadow disk area vs total sphere.
Animate rotation to keep shadow constant [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg].

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaway
lecture_lines: The sphere's projected shadow is pi r squared.
Its total surface area is four times that.
Projection provides a 2D constraint on 3D volume.
